newsitem.title: USA: EMS/Mark firms as dlr/mark hit by stock slide.
newsitem.headline: EMS/Mark firms as dlr/mark hit by stock slide.

text.p: 1445 GMT - Mark at session highs on crosses in late trade as buoyed by dollar/mark's sharp retreat from 1.80 following news of widening U.S. trade deficit and sharp slide in Dow index.
* Dow down 1.8 pct in early U.S. after trade report and amid jitters in Latin American markets.
* Lira underperforms on crosses, with mark/lira probing above 974. Punt retreats as revaluation speculation fades.
* Traders wary of heavy mark bids at 1.80 per dollar and also eyeing French public accounts audit due early Monday. Temptation to cover overextended short-mark positions growing.

* Traders still wary of Bundesbank draining liqiudity/ nudging up market interest rates. Buba's Zeitler says M3 should be watched closely in light of surging stock markets. Palm says sees no reason to switch to variable rate repos right now.
* German Ifo index rises to 96.0 in June vs 95.4.
* Mark/Paris at 3.3790/95 vs 3.3785/90 in Europe late Thursday. Mark/lira at 974.00/40 vs 972.30/60.

* Punt edges back from ERM limits vs French franc, now 12.03 pct vs 12.50 Thursday. Irish FinMin McCreevy reiterates committment to start EMU without UK but declines comment on punt. EU official says punt not on monetary committee agenda.
